question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Jack took on three jobs at once but soon realised he had _____________.

options.text: taken it with a grain of salt
bitten off more than he could chew

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"bitten off more than he could chew"** means to take on more responsibility than one can handle. (अपनी क्षमता से अधिक जिम्मेदारी लेना)

 
 
• **Example: **John realized he had** bitten off more than he could chew **when he agreed to manage three projects at once.
 
 

Therefore, the correct word for fill in the blanks is **'bitten off more than he could chew'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Cut corners** (कोनों को काटना): To do something in the easiest or cheapest way, often sacrificing quality.

 
 
• **Example:** The builder **cut corners **by using low-quality materials, which led to many problems later on.
 
 
 
• **Taken it with a grain of salt** (नमक के साथ लेना): To view something with skepticism or not to take it literally.
 
 
• **Example:** She** took his advice with a grain of salt**, knowing he often exaggerates.
 
 
 
• **Played by the ear** (कान से खेला): To improvise or do something without preparation.
 
 
• **Example:** We didn't have a plan for the meeting, so we just** played it by ear.**
 
 

3f:Tb01,

The correct answer is **Option 1)**
